what: ORIX is a Japanese financial conglomerate. It leases equipment, provides corporate finance, invests in private equity and real estate, runs an asset management business, owns a regional bank and an insurer, and even operates airports and renewable energy projects.
customers: Japanese small and medium businesses, corporate borrowers, insurance policyholders and institutional investors worldwide.
money: Corporate Financial Services and Maintenance Leasing
equipment leasing and lending in Japan
private equity, asset management and overseas businesses
moat: A long record of recycling capital between very different businesses, backed by relationships with Japanese small firms that few foreign competitors can reach.
risks: The conglomerate structure makes it hard to value and often trades at a discount
Return on invested capital of about 3% reflects a balance-sheet-heavy business
Japanese rate rises raise its own funding costs
Only one analyst covers it in this data
opportunities: Revenue grew about 9% last year with a 13% net margin
Asset sales regularly release gains it can return to shareholders
Japanese corporate governance reform is pushing companies to simplify and return capital
watch: Segment profit by business and the pace of asset recycling.
